title: Part I Protheoria: Formula of Discord — Frederick III, Predestination ulcer, hardening causes
pass_a_gloss: Continues through Germany: rise even vs best/most pious Princes — fierce storm vs Frederick III Palatine; firebrands chiefly J. Andreae, Heshusius, Bidenbach, to shut pious Frederick from Peace of Religion + Augsburg Confession society; frustrated at Augsburg Diet 1566. Formula Concordiae finishes it (first Torgau, then Bergen) — truly Discordiae Formula + lasting Schism complement; Elector Ludwig Palatine protests at once though Lutheran-devoted, plus other Princes + weighty Theologians (Hospinian, Alting already praised). But Predestination Controv. + annexed heads (via Sam. Huber then Aegid. Hunnius Wittenberg circa 1580; Calixtus on Thorn Confess. p.14) draws ulcer wider/incurable. Harden Evangelical dissent to this day: Satan kakotechnia; Jesuit occult arts; Politicians serving Rome/self; Theologians kakozelia, typhus, hatreds, calumnies, prejudices, eristic virulent writings, private studia — ends only when Most Serene Princes authority + greater force (if ever) coerce.
pass_b_english: through Germany — so far that they rose even against the best and most pious Princes: as when a fierce tempest was stirred against Frederick III of the Palatinate, with Jakob Andreae, Heshusius, and Bidenbach as chief firebrands, that they might shut pious Frederick out of the Peace of Religion and the Society of the Augsburg Confession — though they would fail at the Augsburg Diet of 1566. At last the Formula of Concord finished the work — first the Torgau Formula, afterward the Bergen — of which we have just spoken: in truth a Formula of Discord, and the complement of a lasting Schism. Elector Ludwig of the Palatinate protested at once, though most devoted to the Lutherans, and other Princes with him, and also the weightiest Theologians — Hospinian, Alting, and the rest already praised at length. But the unhappy Controversy concerning Predestination and its annexed Heads, born chiefly through Samuel Huber and then through Aegidius Hunnius of Wittenberg around the year 1580 — or so Georg Calixtus testifies below on the Confession of Thorn, p. 14 — drew the ulcer wider and rendered it incurable.

And at last they have hardened that Evangelical dissent down to this very day: Satan's malign craft (κακοτεχνία); the hidden arts of the many-scheming Jesuits (τῶν πολυμηχάνων); the calculations of Politicians who serve Rome or their own advantage; and among Theologians for the most part a spiteful rivalry (κακοζηλία), pride, hatreds, calumnies, prejudices, eristic and virulent writings, and private ambitions in very many cases — as it happens — and it will have no end until, by the authority of the Most Serene Princes and by a greater force if one ever intervenes, they are coerced.
source_text: per Germaniam; adeo ut etiam in optimos pientissimosque Principes insurgerent, qualiter in Fridericum III. Palatinum atrox tempestas excitata, incentoribus praecipue J. Andreae, Heshusio, Bidenbachio, ut scilicet Fridericum Pium Pace Religionis, & Societate Augustanae Confess. excluderent, frustra futuri in Comitiis Augustanis A. 1566. Absolvit ultimo Formula Concordiae primo Torgensis, Bergensis postea, de qua modo dictum, re vera Discordiae Formula, & duraturi Schismatis Complementum; reclamaturis statim, Ludovico Elect. Palatino, Lutheranis quanquam addictissimo, aliisque Principibus, sed & Theologis gravissimis, ut fuse laudati Hospinianus, Altingius, &c. Sed diduxit ulcus in majus ac insanabile reddidit infelix Controversia de Praedestinatione, & annexis Capitibus nata praecipue, per Sam. Huberum, tum per Aegid. Hunnium Wittenbergensem, circa A. 1580. vel teste infra Georgio Calixto ad Confessionem Thorunensem, p. 14. Ac tandem obfirmarunt in hunc usque diem Evangelicor. istud dissidium, Satanae κακοτεχνία; occultae Jesuitarum artes τῶν πολυμηχάνων; Politicorum rationes Romae servientium, aut commodis suis; ac Theologorum plerumque κακοζηλία, typhus, odia, calumniae, praejudicia, scripta eristica & virulenta, ac privata in plurimis studia, ut accidit, nec habitura finem, donec Serenissimorum Principum auctoritate, ac vi majore, si interveniat unquam, coerceantur.
